articles.title: Regiões da capital paulista em que Haddad e Tarcísio mais tiveram votos são mais populosas do que 5.189 cidades do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: O Brasil tem 5.571 municípios. Distrito de Piraporinha, na Zona Sul da capital, concentrou 89.458 votos no petista; em Indianópolis, Tarcísio recebeu 88.468 votos, mais do que o total de moradores de 5.189 cidades do país. Veja como foi a votação em cada região.
articles.summary: O Brasil tem 5.571 municípios. Distrito de Piraporinha, na Zona Sul da capital, concentrou 89.458 votos no petista; em Indianópolis, Tarcísio recebeu 88.468 votos, mais do que o total de moradores de 5.189 cidades do país. Veja como foi a votação em cada região.
articles.body:
Tarcísio de Freitas e Fernando Haddad — Foto: Reprodução

O candidato ao governo Fernanda Haddad (PT) conquistou 89.458 votos na 372ª Zona Eleitoral da capital, em Piraporinha, na Zona Sul. O número é superior à população de 5.191 dos 5.571 municípios brasileiros , segundo dados do IBGE em 2026.

Entre os municípios brasileiros, o mais próximo desse total é Quixadá, a 10ª cidade mais populosa do Ceará, com 89.190 habitantes. A diferença é de 268 pessoas.

Do lado de Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), a maior votação absoluta na capital foi registrada na 258ª Zona Eleitoral, em Indianópolis, onde o governador reeleito recebeu 88.468 votos. Esse total é superior à população de 5.189 municípios brasileiros.

A cidade com população mais próxima desse número é Concórdia, a 17ª mais populosa de Santa Catarina, com 88.402 habitantes. A diferença é de 66 pessoas.

Indianópolis já havia aparecido como destaque no recorte proporcional da votação na capital. Foi ali também que Tarcísio registrou seu melhor desempenho percentual em São Paulo, com 66,48% dos votos válidos.

Na capital paulista, a 1ª Zona Eleitoral, na Bela Vista, foi a que Haddad teve maior votação proporcional, com 58,96% dos votos válidos. Depois de Piraporinha, as maiores votações absolutas de Haddad na capital foram registradas em:

No caso de Tarcísio, Indianópolis concentrou ao mesmo tempo sua maior votação absoluta e seu maior percentual na cidade. Depois dos 88.468 votos registrados em Indianópolis, as maiores votações do governador foram:

Governador reeleito no estado, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) venceu Fernando Haddad (PT) em 38 das 57 zonas eleitorais da capital paulista nas eleições deste domingo (4). O candidato petista venceu em apenas 19 zonas eleitorais da capital ( confira tabela abaixo ).

Tarcísio ganhou na capital por 52,76% contra 46,09% do petista. Já Lula venceu na capital paulista.

Considerando o percentual obtido por cada candidato, Tarcísio teve seu melhor resultado em Indianópolis, onde alcançou 66,48% dos votos. Já Haddad teve seu maior percentual na Bela Vista, com 58,96%.

Em relação aos números absolutos, Indianópolis também foi a zona em que Tarcísio recebeu mais votos (88.468). No caso de Haddad, a maior votação foi registrada em Piraporinha, com 89.458 votos.

A 258ª Zona Eleitoral, em Indianópolis, foi onde Tarcísio teve seu melhor desempenho proporcional na capital. Ele recebeu 66,48% dos votos, contra 32,81% de Haddad.

O segundo maior percentual do governador foi registrado no Tatuapé, com 65,94%. Em seguida aparecem Mooca, com 64,59%; Santana, com 63,46%; Vila Formosa, com 63,22%; Santo Amaro, com 62,98%; Jardim Paulista, com 62,52%; Vila Maria, com 62,09%; Vila Prudente, com 60,96%; e Vila Sabrina, com 60,73%.

Ao todo, Tarcísio superou os 60% em dez zonas eleitorais.

Entre as zonas em que Haddad venceu, a maior proporção de votos foi registrada na Bela Vista. Na 1ª Zona Eleitoral, o petista teve 58,96%, enquanto Tarcísio ficou com 39,95%.

Piraporinha aparece logo depois, com 58,45% para Haddad, seguida por Cidade Tiradentes, com 58,25%; Valo Velho, com 57,43%; Grajaú, com 57,30%; e Parelheiros, com 56,13%.

Haddad ultrapassou os 50% dos votos em Capão Redondo, com 54,51%; Guaianases, com 53,16%; São Mateus, com 52,78%; Conjunto José Bonifácio, com 51,70%; Campo Limpo, com 51,35%; Jardim São Luís, com 50,96%; Itaim Paulista, com 50,66%; Perus, com 50,39%; Jardim Helena, com 50,39%; e Brasilândia, com 50,38%.

A tabela também mostra zonas eleitorais em que os dois candidatos ficaram muito próximos.

A menor diferença percentual aparece no Jaraguá, onde Haddad teve 49,41%, e Tarcísio 49,25%, uma diferença de apenas 0,16%;

articles.title: Senadora eleita por RR Teresa Surita quer combater crise na saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-prefeita da capital cobra reestruturação no atendimento médico e promete atuar pela infraestrutura básica dos municípios durante bate-papo após vitória nas urnas.
articles.summary: Ex-prefeita da capital cobra reestruturação no atendimento médico e promete atuar pela infraestrutura básica dos municípios durante bate-papo após vitória nas urnas.
articles.body:
Senadora eleita por Roraima nas eleições de 2026, Teresa Surita (MDB) , afirmou que a eficiência na gestão pública será o foco do mandato e classificou a área da saúde como "prioridade zero" .

A declaração foi dada na primeira entrevista após a eleição, na manhã desta terça-feira (6), no Bom Dia Roraima , da Rede Amazônica .

Ex-prefeita de Boa Vista , Teresa conquistou a segunda vaga do estado ao Senado, com mais de 117 mil votos , o que representa mais de 19% dos votos válidos . Ao destacar os principais problemas de Roraima, a política focou na necessidade de melhorar a aplicação do orçamento público .

"A nossa questão da saúde é prioridade zero. [...] Não pode faltar remédio, material cirúrgico, atenção aos profissionais nem médicos. Tudo isso é o serviço público que tem que oferecer. Não é falta de recurso, é falta de uma estratégia", afirmou a senadora eleita.

Ela também destacou que pretende atuar de forma independente em Brasília. O objetivo, segundo ela, é adotar uma postura sem palanques políticos para defender exclusivamente as demandas da população roraimense.

Entre as pautas de desenvolvimento, Teresa Surita afirmou que há o déficit crítico de saneamento básico fora da capital . Ela ressaltou que há municípios no interior do estado onde apenas 20% dos moradores têm acesso a água tratada e quase não existe rede de esgoto .

Para a infraestrutura, a parlamentar prometeu articular a abertura de uma estrada que ligaria o município de Caroebe , no Sul do estado, ao Pará. Segundo ela, a via de acesso será um grande corredor econômico e de desenvolvimento para a região.

Senadora eleita por Roraima, Teresa Surita (MDB) concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Roraima nesta terça (6). — Foto: Rede Amazônica

No campo social, a senadora eleita definiu como meta para os primeiros 100 dias de mandato a criação de uma legislação mais rígida para proteger mulheres . A medida busca combater os altos índices de feminicídio registrados em Roraima e garantir punições mais severas aos agressores.

A política também se comprometeu a atuar em defesa das mães atípicas e a trabalhar em cooperação com todos os prefeitos do estado.

Na área da educação, Teresa defendeu um planejamento estruturado voltado aos jovens. Ela afirmou que a melhoria do ensino exige ações profundas e vai além de apenas reformar os prédios escolares.

O Bom Dia Roraima entrevistou os dois senadores eleitos por Roraima nas Eleições 2026. Na última segunda-feira (5) Nicoletti (PL) , o mais votado do pleito no estado, falou sobre zerar filas de cirurgias e destinar 50% das emendas parlamentares à saúde.

articles.title: Óculos inteligentes: Países avaliam restrições por privacidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Governos e empresas analisam novas regras para impedir que dispositivos com câmeras e microfones sejam usados para registrar pessoas ou informações sem autorização.
articles.summary: Óculos inteligentes enfrentam barreiras em diversos países que buscam impedir gravações sem autorização em tribunais, escolas e espaços públicos de grande circulação.
articles.body:
Óculos inteligente tem câmera, sensor e componentes eletrônicos instalados na armação e nas hastes. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Governos, tribunais e empresas de diferentes países estão avaliando restrições aos óculos inteligentes diante de preocupações com a privacidade.

A tecnologia, popularizada pelos modelos Ray-Ban da Meta , permite fotografar, gravar vídeos e captar áudios. Autoridades temem que os dispositivos sejam usados para registrar pessoas ou informações confidenciais sem consentimento.

Veja o que alguns países e regiões estão fazendo:

O governo federal avalia proibir o uso de óculos inteligentes com câmeras em locais de trabalho públicos por razões de privacidade e segurança.

A ministra do Serviço Público, Katy Gallagher, pediu uma avaliação sobre a necessidade de proibição e possíveis exceções.

Tribunais da Inglaterra e do País de Gales proibiram o uso de óculos inteligentes da Meta por causa das restrições à gravação de imagens e vídeos nas cortes.

Cinemas britânicos também estão adotando regras para proibir ou limitar o uso de dispositivos com câmeras.

Autoridades europeias de proteção de dados e parlamentares estão analisando os riscos dos óculos inteligentes.

O Comitê Europeu de Proteção de Dados encomendou um relatório sobre a "aceitação social" da tecnologia. Uma eurodeputada também pediu que a Comissão Europeia avalie possíveis medidas.

O governo pretende propor uma proibição temporária de óculos com inteligência artificial em locais públicos de grande circulação, como parques, praias, museus, centros comerciais e eventos.

Em agosto, Oslo, capital do país, proibiu o uso de óculos inteligentes nas escolas.

O Sistema Judiciário Unificado de Nova York proibiu os óculos inteligentes em todas as suas instalações desde 20 de julho.

A regra vale para óculos de grau e sem grau e acessórios com câmeras, microfones, computadores ou outras tecnologias capazes de gravar áudio e vídeo.

Visitantes precisam entregar os dispositivos aos funcionários dos tribunais antes de entrar.

articles.title: Rubio na Islândia: país é central para segurança dos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretário de Estado americano afirmou que Washington está aberto a ampliar a cooperação com o país diante do crescimento de ameaças militares, econômicas e de infraestrutura na região.
articles.summary: Rubio na Islândia propõe ampliar cooperação militar e econômica para enfrentar ameaças no Ártico e reforçar a segurança estratégica do Atlântico Norte.
articles.body:
O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, conversa com a ministra das Relações Exteriores da Islândia, Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir. — Foto: Mark Schiefelbein/Pool via REUTERS

O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio , afirmou nesta terça-feira (6) que a Islândia ocupa uma posição estratégica para a segurança do Atlântico Norte e do Ártico. Segundo ele, Washington está aberto a ampliar a cooperação com o país diante do aumento das ameaças na região.

Rubio falou durante uma visita à Islândia, ao lado da ministra das Relações Exteriores do país, Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir.

"A Islândia está no centro de muitas das questões relacionadas à segurança e à defesa da nossa região compartilhada", afirmou Rubio.

O secretário de Estado citou preocupações com ameaças militares, econômicas e relacionadas à infraestrutura no extremo norte. Ele também destacou a localização geográfica da Islândia e o papel do país para as operações militares americanas.

Segundo Rubio, a Islândia permite que os Estados Unidos utilizem seu território, espaço aéreo e águas como um ponto estratégico para monitorar atividades clandestinas e dissuadir adversários.

"Estaríamos abertos a ter essas conversas para ver o que mais podemos fazer juntos. Sei que há interesse em fazer mais juntos", disse.

Rubio também afirmou que a posição da Islândia é importante não apenas para a defesa da Europa, mas também para a segurança dos Estados Unidos.

"A Islândia e sua localização desempenham um papel fundamental na defesa tanto da Europa quanto do território dos Estados Unidos, por causa da geografia", afirmou.

Presidente americano publicou uma imagem em que toda a América do Norte e a Groenlândia aparecem com a bandeira dos Estados Unidos. — Foto: Reprodução/Truth Social/@realDonaldTrump

Em setembro, o país entrou na mira de Donald Trump. O presidente americano publicou nas redes sociais uma imagem que mostra a ilha e outros países cobertos pela bandeira americana.

O mapa mostrava os Estados Unidos, o Canadá, a Groenlândia, a Islândia, o México, a América Central e o Caribe cobertos pela bandeira dos EUA. Toda a área terrestre aparece identificada como "Estados Unidos da América".

Trump publicou a imagem em sua plataforma Truth Social sem apresentar explicações.

A ministra das Relações Exteriores da Islândia, Thorgerdur Gunnarsdottir, convocou Billy Long, embaixador dos EUA no país, para explicar a publicação.

As declarações de Trump nos últimos anos de que os Estados Unidos deveriam adquirir a Groenlândia, território dinamarquês semiautônomo, provocaram tensões entre Washington e Copenhague, ambos membros fundadores da Otan, e de forma mais ampla em toda a Europa.

Em agosto, a Islândia votou contra a retomada das negociações para ingressar na União Europeia em um referendo no qual as intenções de Trump em relação à Groenlândia serviram como pano de fundo.

articles.title: EUA cobram da Rússia sobre morte de pesquisadora de instituto de peste | G1
articles.standfirst: Morte gerou temor no país por uma nova onda de peste. Moscou descartou que doença tenha sido a causa da morte da pesquisadora, mas secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, disse querer provas.
articles.summary: Morte gerou temor no país por uma nova onda de peste. Moscou descartou que doença tenha sido a causa da morte da pesquisadora, mas secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, disse querer provas.
articles.body:
Vista do Centro de Assistência Médica e Resgate, na região de Irkutsk, na Rússia, em 5 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters

O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos , Marco Rubio , disse nesta terça-feira (6) que a Rússia deveria compartilhar mais informações sobre a morte de uma funcionária do laboratório do Instituto da Peste, ocorrida na semana passada.

➡️ Segundo a rede de TV estatal local, a mulher morreu após contrair pneumonia de causa "desconhecida" . A Rússia disse que a peste foi descartada , mas não revelou a causa da morte, o que gerou uma onda de temor no país por um novo surto da doença.

Na segunda-feira (5), o governo russo insistiu que a situação está sob controle . Ainda assim, Rubio pediu que a Rússia forneça mais detalhes do episódio e disse que Washington está acompanhando o caso “muito de perto”.

“Acho que cabe à Rússia , obviamente, compartilhar mais informações com o mundo”, disse Rubio a repórteres durante visita à Islândia. “Estamos acompanhando a situação muito de perto, hora a hora".

Também nesta terça-feira (6), a imprensa russa relatou uma nova morte, também por causas suspeitas, no mesmo hospital em que a pesquisadora estava internada, na região de Irkutsk, no sudeste da Sibéria.

Nenhuma autoridade havia se manifestado sobre a suposta segunda morte até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Pesquisadores trabalham em laboratório do Instituto Irkutsk de Pesquisa Antipraga da Sibéria e do Oriente, em imagem de 2019. — Foto: Instituto Irkutsk de Pesquisa Antipraga da Sibéria e do Oriente via AP

A mulher que morreu na semana passada trabalhava no Instituto de Pesquisa Antipeste da Sibéria e do Extremo Oriente, em Irkutsk. O hospital em que ela esteve internada foi colocado em quarentena.

A agência sanitária russa informou no domingo (4) que a mulher havia sido diagnosticada com "pneumonia de etiologia [origem] desconhecida" e declarou que testes "extensos" não detectaram "nenhum microrganismo associado às atividades profissionais da paciente".

A agência também afirmou não ter encontrado incidentes no instituto "envolvendo microrganismos patogênicos".

articles.title: EUA e China negociam visitas mútuas a instalações nucleares, diz TV | G1
articles.standfirst: Tratativas preliminares ocorreram dias após visita de Xi Jinping à Casa Branca e em meio a temores de nova corrida nuclear armamentista entre potências mundiais.
articles.summary: Tratativas preliminares ocorreram dias após visita de Xi Jinping à Casa Branca e em meio a temores de nova corrida nuclear armamentista entre potências mundiais.
articles.body:
Os presidentes da China, Xi Jinping, e dos EUA, Donald Trump, em cerimônia na Casa Branca, nos Estados Unidos, em 24 de setembro de 2025. — Foto: Evan Vucci/ Reuters

Os Estados Unidos e China estão negociando visitas mútuas a suas instalações nucleares, revelou nesta terça-feira (6) a TV CNN Internacional.

Foram discutidas visitas aos laboratórios nacionais do Departamento de Energia dos EUA e a instalações equivalentes na China, e os EUA estariam dispostos a discutir visitas a locais de testes nucleares, disseram autoridades do governo norte-americano ao veículo.

No entanto, as conversas sobre o assunto que ocorreram até o momento foram tratadas como "iniciais e preliminares" , segundo as fontes de Washington. Mesmo assim, o governo Trump pretende continuar pressionando Pequim nos próximos meses por novas rodadas de tratativas sobre o assunto, ainda segundo a TV.

A revelação ocorre dias após visita de Xi Jinping à Casa Branca e também em meio a temores de nova corrida nuclear armamentista entre potências mundiais após o fim do New START —tratado de não proliferação de armas nucleares entre EUA e Rússia que expirou em fevereiro.

O governo Trump busca incluir a China em qualquer novo acordo para limitar a produção e posicionamento de armas nucleares , segundo disse Trump à época do fim do New START. Isso porque Pequim expande rapidamente seu arsenal atômico , apesar de ter cerca de 10% da quantidade de ogivas que EUA e Rússia, segundo o Instituto Internacional de Pesquisa da Paz de Estocolmo (Sipri).

A ideia de visitas recíprocas foi inicialmente levantada pelos chineses durante uma reunião com autoridades norte-americanas neste ano , disse uma fonte à CNN Internacional. Isso foi interpretado por Washington como uma indicação de que o país asiático estaria aberto a adotar medidas em prol de construir confiança entre os dois países na pauta nuclear para, no futuro, construir um acordo mais abrangente.

Mísseis balísticos JL-3, de alcance intercontinental e lançados por submarinos, mostrados em desfile militar na China em setembro de 2025. — Foto: REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

articles.title: Protestos na França: premiê condena violência em atos estudantis | G1
articles.standfirst: Pelo menos 715 policiais e 215 adolescentes já ficaram feridos em confrontos durante as manifestações, que atingiram sua maior mobilização nesta terça (6).
articles.summary: Pelo menos 715 policiais e 215 adolescentes já ficaram feridos em confrontos durante as manifestações, que atingiram sua maior mobilização nesta terça (6).
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro da França , Sébastien Lecornu, afirmou nesta terça-feira (6) que "não pode haver espaço para tolerância à violência" ao falar sobre os protestos estudantis que vem reunindo milhares de estudantes pelas ruas em todo o país.

Em discurso no Parlamento, o premiê francês condenou atos de vandalismo que vêm sendo praticados e disse que eles pioram ainda mais a situação das escolas - os manifestantes apontam a precariedade da infraestrutura de várias delas como motivação.

"Incendiar uma escola secundária não melhora o estado dos edifícios escolares. Linchar um professor não ajuda a substituir professores", disse ele ao parlamento, acrescentando que era uma "mentira" sugerir que o governo havia ordenado "repressão policial" contra os manifestantes.

Os protestos estudantis começaram em setembro na região de Paris e rapidamente se espalharam por todo o país entre os alunos. Segundo as autoridades francesas, esta terça é o dia de maior mobilização até o momento, com cerca de 256 mil pessoas nas ruas.

Em Marselha , Nantes e Lyon, os protestos de rua começaram pacificamente no meio da manhã, mas em Estrasburgo, Lyon e Rennes, eles tornaram-se violentos, com a polícia disparando gás lacrimogêneo contra os manifestantes, que atearam fogo nas ruas e lançaram projéteis.

A maior manifestação está prevista para ocorrer na capital do país, Paris, à tarde.

De acordo com a União dos Estudantes do Ensino Médio, 1.800 escolas estão bloqueadas ou fecharão durante o dia.

Apesar das críticas, segundo a agência de notícias Reuters, Lecornu ordenou que seus ministros atendam às principais reivindicações dos estudantes e enviem propostas para as melhorias até o fim do mês . Entre as medidas que devem ser tomadas está:

garantir a substituição de professores ausentes

rever a duração do dia letivo - das 8h às 18h

Alunos da França fazem protestos com foto em Saint-Denis, próximo a Paris. — Foto: Abdul Saboor/Reuters

Faz duas semanas que esses protestos vêm ocorrendo. Os manifestantes reclamam de jornadas excessivamente longas, de condições inadequadas nas salas de aula (quentes demais no verão, por exemplo) e de ausências excessivas de professores.

Após começarem na periferia de Paris, as manifestações vêm se tornando violentas. Diversos confrontos entre manifestantes e policiais foram registrados, e milhares de estudantes foram detidos pela polícia.

O Ministério do Interior da França diz que 6.100 pessoas foram presas desde o início dos protestos, sendo a esmagadora maioria delas menores de idade . Mais de 1.800 estão sendo processadas, incluindo 1.483 menores, informou o Ministério da Justiça.

O chefe da polícia de Paris afirmou durante o fim de semana que os protestos estudantis na capital francesa estavam "fora de controle".

Pelo menos 715 policiais e 215 adolescentes ficaram feridos nos confrontos, segundo o gabinete do primeiro-ministro francês.

Nesta segunda-feira (5), um estudante de 15 anos teve a mão arrancada em Lens , no norte da França. O incidente ocorreu após ele pegar uma granada de efeito moral da polícia, que explodiu quando ele tentava arremessá-la de volta na direção dos agentes , afirmou uma fonte ligada ao sindicato dos policiais à agência de notícias AFP.

Os amplos protestos causaram uma crise política para o governo de Emmanuel Macron. A mídia francesa afirmou que o presidente estaria "apavorado" com a crise. Oficialmente, Macron reconhece que as reivindicações do movimento são legítimas, mas a violência, não.

articles.title: Meet Ben Hogan, former bike mechanic turning discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs; shares free instructions online to help others recreate the design locally
articles.summary: A Michigan man has been turning discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs while also teaching others how to make them, all for free.
articles.body: A Michigan man has been turning discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs while also teaching others how to make them, all for free. Ben Hogan, a former bike mechanic and prosthetist at Mary Free Bed Rehabilitation Hospital, founded Project Bike Leg, an initiative that makes prosthetics sourced almost entirely from repurposed bike parts. He hopes his low-cost design can eventually help millions of amputees around the world, according to a report by PEOPLE's Toria Sheffield.Hogan worked at the Michigan State University Bikes Service Centre as a student 20 years ago, where he learned to repair bikes. Bike shop general manager Tim Potter trained Hogan. “When I think about it, you know, I mean, it sometimes will tear you up,” said Potter.Hogan revealed that it all began with a random encounter. “I had a chance encounter with an amputee that walked into a bike shop I was working at in Los Angeles in 2011,” he said to the outlet. “He showed me his prosthesis unprompted, and it really informed me of how much a bike and a prosthesis had in common.” “After [later] shadowing some prosthetists at UCLA, I made the connection that it was my calling,” he added.Moreover, he shared that his desire to create something both functional and cost-efficient only grew after he learned how many amputees worldwide do not have access to the prosthetics they need. Citing World Health Organisation estimates, Hogan said that a "staggering 85-90% of amputees worldwide lack access to a proper prosthesis." “As a former bike mechanic turned prosthetist, I was naturally drawn to take a bicycle and turn it into a prosthesis,” he said. “A bike, after all, is a tool used to enhance human locomotion. The inherent design would allow for an adjustable, lightweight, structurally sound and functional prosthesis.”After seriously working and experimenting with the designs, Hogan crafted his first below-the-knee prosthesis model within a few weeks in 2013. However, he said he decided to put the project aside until he had developed his skillset more fully. “Due to the fact that I had not yet achieved a master's vantage point of the prosthetic arts, I decided to set the bike leg down until I could say that I honestly had the advanced prosthetic skillset to ‘reinvent the wheel’ of prosthetic care,” he explained.It was in the summer of 2024 that he decided he was finally ready to return to the initiative, at which point he officially founded Project Bike Leg. “I had been working at Mary Free Bed Rehabilitation Hospital for the past 8 years and had a patient who was up for the challenge. Using all of the rudimentary concepts of prosthetics that I had come to know in the previous decade, I crafted a new design of a BK [below-the-knee] bike leg that had an enhanced level of adjustability and functionality compared to the previous model.”Andy Leedom, who lost his leg five years ago in a car accident, is one of Hogan’s bike-leg testers. Leedom is on his third prosthesis, which cost nearly $70,000. “I call myself the guinea pig,” Leedom said. “Ben’s been to enough places that he knows what is needed.”He went on to design an above-the-knee model in 2025 and decided he felt ready to share his designs on a larger scale. The prosthetic is made from over 95% bicycle parts. The foot is formed from a bike seat, strips of wheel and tyre treads, held together with spokes. The seat post and frame add stability. “If you look at the back of the knee, there are two chains,” Hogan said. “These hold the knee stable and there are two of them.”The cable used to shift gears runs around the bike-leg to hold it together. The socket is made of wicker, which local communities could make out of material they have access to. “It’s actually a perfect application for a prosthesis, because it’s already built to take the weight of a human, so all I’ve done is reconfigure it in a different way to be a prosthesis,” Hogan said.He soon met with a physician in Ghana, where he eventually travelled to personally teach prosthetics students how to recreate his designs. He shared that by the end of his nine-day trip he and the students had successfully completed their work on building two fully-made prosthetics and given two amputees the ability to walk again. “And now they can train others in the Ghana region on how to make bike legs,” Hogan said.“This was a phenomenal experience that I will never forget, and I cannot wait to see what the local clinicians might do with the bike legs moving forward,” he said of the experience.Moreover, he is training thousands more across the globe on how to make their own prosthetic legs with the help of his website. He shares instructional videos on how to make both above-the-knee and below-the-knee bike leg prosthetics, with pages of pictures and step-by-step instructions.In a recent conversation with InvestigateTV about the project, Hogan said he has no intention to patent the design or personally profit from it. “I don’t have any intention of financially benefiting from it or patenting these designs,” he told the outlet. “I want them to be available to all parties all over the world.”For Hogan, the next step is a pilot study with amputees in third-world countries wearing bike legs full time. He hopes his invention will eventually help some of the 30 to 40 million people worldwide who need prosthetic legs.“As my sister said, your career should be your greatest gift to the world,” he said, “and I do think this is my greatest gift to the world.”You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1968, Jeff McKissack began building Houston’s Orange Show from salvaged materials, creating a unique folk art landmark that opened to the public in 1979
articles.summary: In October 1977, William Martin wrote in Texas Monthly that the Orange Show, a folk art site on Munger Street in southeast Houston, was the passion of its
articles.body: In October 1977, William Martin wrote in Texas Monthly that the Orange Show, a folk art site on Munger Street in southeast Houston, was the passion of its creator, Jeff McKissack, then 75. McKissack told William Martin in a Texas Monthly interview, "I work on it every day." The complex, built from salvaged materials, honours oranges, which McKissack saw as symbols of strength, purity and the American way. McKissack opened the show to the public in 1979, and it is now a pilgrimage destination for folk art lovers worldwide. This article traces its creation, collection, recognition and preservation.How did McKissack build the Orange ShowMcKissack built the show largely from salvaged and bought items. Some came from buildings demolished in downtown Houston during his years at the Post Office. They included roof tiles from the old Capitol Theatre, a railing from a Stowers Furniture Company fire escape and a miniature obelisk from the Texas State Hotel. Other pieces came from antique and junk shops between Houston and Hot Springs, Arkansas, where McKissack had holidayed since 1918. Cast-iron tractor seats and dozens of buggy wheels were his most successful finds, and they served as seating and as decoration on gates, fences and partitions.The exhibits described included a steamboat display, a steam buggy and an exhibit room roughly eight feet wide and twenty feet long. The room held mannequin scenes, a tepee and signs with McKissack's own wording. McKissack told Martin he had at least $10,000 worth of further exhibits stored in his living room. He also said that he had worked on the project since 1968: "I started working on it in 1968, and I work on it every day."Why did Harithas support the Orange ShowJames Harithas, director of the Contemporary Arts Museum, first visited the Orange Show in 1975 and became an enthusiastic supporter. Harithas said he took visitors to see it, among them the painter Willem de Kooning and the collector Count Panza, and called it the "Orange Shrine". His visits were interrupted when the Bicentennial flood destroyed the museum in June 1976.Harithas told Martin he doubted the show would bring McKissack substantial income unless it was sold as a work of art to a collector who would maintain it. He estimated it could fetch a few hundred thousand dollars. If no sale came about, he felt the city should take it over as a monument, and he said he intended to put the museum behind it. McKissack's own hope was for 100,000 to 300,000 visitors a year. Neighbourhood boys had broken in shortly before his last visit, pouring paint over the exhibit room and damaging exhibits. McKissack told him he had scolded the boys but had not told their parents.How large was the Orange ShowAccording to the Texas Historical Foundation, a grant presentation to the Orange Show Foundation on 27 June 2023. Working as a postal worker by day and an artist by night. By the time he opened the show to the public more than twenty years later, it said, he had assembled salvaged materials into 3,000 square feet of sculptural environment. It states that he opened it in 1979 and that it survived less than a year afterwards.The grant came from its William Jack Sibley Arts Endowment. It supports ongoing efforts to restore and maintain the site, whose oldest parts are approaching 70 years old. The foundation said the piecemeal nature of the original work makes maintenance complex, requiring fidelity to both aesthetic and structural integrity. It described the Orange Show as a pilgrimage destination for lovers of folk art around the world.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A $2.35 million security project at North Dakota’s governor’s residence uncovered human remains; archaeologists have now removed 7 coffins after examining more than 80 areas around the construction site
articles.summary: A routine security upgrade at North Dakota’s governor’s residence has opened an unexpected window into Bismarck’s past.
articles.body: A routine security upgrade at North Dakota’s governor’s residence has opened an unexpected window into Bismarck’s past. What began as a $2.35 million project to improve fencing and access around the property turned into an archaeological investigation after construction crews uncovered human remains beneath the ground, states an online report by North Dakota Monitor. Months later, archaeologists have removed seven coffins containing human remains, along with an unidentified wooden box, after examining more than 80 areas of interest around the construction site, the report adds.A cemetery beneath modern BismarckThe discovery dates back to May, when workers installing a new fence near the governor’s residence encountered human remains. The location was once part of Bismarck’s first cemetery, which operated between 1873 and 1877. Many of the people originally buried there were later moved to St. Mary’s Cemetery and Fairview Cemetery during the 1880s. The discovery suggests that some burials may have remained behind despite those historic efforts to relocate graves, the report adds.Archaeologists returned to the area in September for a more extensive investigation. Their work covered more than 80 areas identified as potentially significant, eventually leading to the removal of the seven coffins and the wooden box. The findings add another layer to the history of a part of the city that has undergone substantial development since the cemetery was active, adds the report.A careful examination of the remainsThe archaeological work is now moving into its next phase. Researchers will examine and catalogue the remains and other objects recovered during the fieldwork, a process expected to continue into early 2027. The analysis is expected to focus on basic biological information such as estimated age ranges and possible evidence of disease or other conditions that might provide clues to the individuals buried there.DNA testing is not planned as part of the investigation. Instead, archaeologists will rely on physical examination and historical research to better understand the remains and the circumstances surrounding the burials. The unidentified wooden box recovered alongside the coffins will also be examined as researchers work to establish a clearer picture of what was once located on the site.Not the first discovery in the areaHuman remains have been uncovered elsewhere around the North Dakota Capitol grounds over the decades, claims the online report. Previous discoveries occurred during construction of a trolley line near the southwest corner of the Capitol property in 1903. Remains were also found in 1959 while the previous governor’s residence was being constructed. The latest discovery therefore forms part of a longer archaeological story beneath the modern government complex, where layers of Bismarck’s early history remain hidden below later development.Preparing for a respectful reburialAuthorities are taking steps to ensure the recovered remains are handled appropriately. The state has contracted with a local funeral home, while Crisis Care Chaplaincy has offered support during the process. Once the archaeological examination is complete, the remains are expected to be reinterred at a local cemetery in spring, adds the report.The reburial will provide a final resting place for people whose original graves were effectively lost beneath the changing landscape of the city.An unexpected cost to a security projectThe archaeological discovery has also added an unforeseen expense to the governor’s residence project. Lawmakers approved $2.35 million last year for security improvements, including a new perimeter fence and an extension to the driveway.By September 1, archaeological work associated with the discovery was estimated to have cost the state an additional $155,000. The Office of Management and Budget has not yet provided an updated figure following completion of the exhumation work.Images Courtesy: istock and North Dakota MonitorYou use AI every day. articles.title: Meryl Streep made a seven-figure gift to preserve women's history; the museum is using it to bring stories into classrooms and digital media
articles.summary: Meryl Streep has made a seven-figure gift to the National Women’s History Museum as the institution prepares to expand how women’s stories are taught and
articles.body: Meryl Streep has made a seven-figure gift to the National Women’s History Museum as the institution prepares to expand how women’s stories are taught and shared across the United States. The donation will support digital projects designed to take historical material beyond a traditional museum setting, including resources that can be used in classrooms and accessed through online platforms. Streep has been a supporter of the museum making the contribution part of a longer association with its work. The museum is also establishing an annual educator award in her name, with the first recipient due to be recognised in November 2026.Meryl Streep backs a wider effort to preserve women’s historyStreep has supported the National Women’s History Museum for years, making the new contribution an extension of an existing relationship rather than a first association with the institution. Meryl Streep said, “History is shaped not only by those who make it, but by those who ensure it is remembered.”“The National Women’s History Museum has long been a catalyst for bringing forward the stories that deepen our understanding of who we are. I am proud to continue supporting this essential work so that future generations inherit a history that is both truthful and complete.”For an institution whose purpose is to bring women’s contributions into the historical record, the timing also has a practical significance. The museum is preparing to increase its national impact ahead of the United States’ 250th anniversary, when questions about which people and events are represented in the country’s history are likely to receive renewed attention.The museum is putting digital storytelling at the centreA substantial part of the funding will go towards digital-first projects. The aim is to create material that does not depend on someone physically visiting a museum or exhibition to encounter it. That could mean resources being used in a classroom, viewed at home or encountered through the digital services people already use. The museum has described the approach as a way of making its storytelling more flexible and accessible, particularly as it seeks to reach audiences outside its established base. The shift also reflects the practical limits of a traditional museum model. Physical exhibitions can only be visited in particular places and at particular times. Digital resources can travel much further, allowing historical material to be used by teachers and students who may never visit the museum itself.For the National Women’s History Museum, the new funding provides an opportunity to develop that side of its work on a larger scale.Bringing women’s history into classroomsEducation is another clear focus of Streep’s contribution. The museum plans to use its expanded resources to make women’s history more available to teachers, students and communities across the country.The institution will also create the Meryl Streep Educator Award. It will be given each year to an educator whose work advances the teaching of women’s history and makes those stories more accessible in schools or local communities. The first recipient is due to be recognised at the museum’s Women Making History Awards Gala in November 2026. The award gives the donation a direct connection to education rather than leaving it solely as a funding commitment for digital development. It also creates an annual way for the museum to recognise teachers whose work brings historical material into everyday learning.Meryl Streep has backed the museum since its early yearsStreep’s involvement with the National Women’s History Museum predates the latest donation. The museum has identified her as one of its earliest and most consistent supporters. Her own career has also been closely associated with portraying women in film, although the museum’s recognition of her is centred on her support for its educational and historical mission. In announcing the gift, its leadership linked her work as an actor and storyteller with the broader role of preserving and communicating women’s experiences.Susan D. Whiting, chair of the museum’s board, described Streep’s contribution as consistent with the organisation’s emphasis on education, historical representation and access to women’s stories. Streep said the museum helps bring forward accounts that can add to a fuller understanding of the past. Her latest contribution, she said, was intended to support that work for future generations.“As one of the most influential storytellers of our time, Meryl Streep has spent her career illuminating the depth, complexity, and power of women’s lives.”The museum’s plans extend beyond the physical spaceThe National Women’s History Museum has increasingly looked towards digital methods as a way of reaching people beyond a conventional museum audience. The new funding is expected to give those efforts more room to develop. That means the museum’s work will not be limited to presenting information in one location. A teacher could use its material during a lesson, a student could encounter it while researching a subject, and someone at home could explore the same stories independently.The approach also gives the museum more scope to tell stories in different formats. Digital platforms can combine written material with visual storytelling and other forms of presentation, allowing historical subjects to be approached in ways that may not fit easily within a physical exhibition.Frédérique Campagne Irwin, the museum’s president and CEO said, “Meryl Streep understands that storytelling shapes culture, and culture shapes what societies believe is possible.”Looking towards the United States’ 250th anniversaryThe museum is planning its expansion against the backdrop of the United States’ 250th anniversary in 2026. That milestone provides a particular moment for institutions concerned with how American history is recorded and taught.For the National Women’s History Museum, the anniversary is being treated as an opportunity to bring more attention to women whose contributions have formed part of the country’s history. The new investment is intended to help the museum do that on a national scale rather than relying primarily on visitors who can reach a physical museum setting.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A South African consortium led by former Sibanye-Stillwater executive chairman Neal Froneman is exploring a $402 million project to turn a 600-hectare
articles.body: A South African consortium led by former Sibanye-Stillwater executive chairman Neal Froneman is exploring a $402 million project to turn a 600-hectare farmland into a Formula 1 circuit in order to bring racing back to the country by 2031, as per a report by Business Tech.Blue Mountain Racing has secured about 600 hectares in Swartland, near Cape Town for a proposed Formula One standard Circuit and wider hospitality, entertainment and property development. The proposal remains at the pre-feasibility stage and has not yet secured a Formula One race, but if successful it would mark South Africa’s return to the championship 38 years after its last Grand Prix at Kyalami in 1993.From mining to motorsportFroneman is best known for his career in South Africa’s mining industry, having led Aflease Gold, which became Gold One, and helped create Uranium One from Aflease’s uranium assets before becoming a prominent gold and platinum executive at Sibanye-Stillwater.But motorsport is also familiar territory for Froneman, a former racing driver, although he said the proposed development is a commercial venture. “I’ve always had a little bit of racing in me, but this is far more about a commercial opportunity,” he said to the local media.Froneman said modern Formula One events require much more than a race track, including capacity for about 125,000 spectators and transport systems capable of moving large crowds into and out of the venue within three hours. This is why, rather than updating the existing Kyalami circuit in Gauteng, Blue Mountain Range, Blue Mountain Racing plans to develop a new facility from scratch in the Western Cape. Froneman said modern Formula One events require much more than a race track, including capacity for about 125,000 spectators and transport systems capable of moving large crowds into and out of the venue within three hours.More than a Formula One circuitThe racing circuit forms just one part of the broader development project that includes a 10,000 square-metre media centre, an amphitheatre and other entertainment facilities. The track would also be designed to host MotoGP and other racing categories, giving the development additional revenue opportunities outside Formula One race weekends.“This is not just going to be a Formula One track. It’s also going to be a MotoGP track,” said Froneman.The location of the project in Cape Town is also banking on its tourism appeal with its wine industry, restaurants, coastline and international visitor base.The project is expected to cost about R6.7 billion ($402 million), with 40% of the funding coming from equity and 60% from debt. Before raising the full amount, however, the developers plan to spend about R120 million ($7.2 million) on seed capital, feasibility studies, environmental approvals, engineering and other preparatory work.“You’re not going to get your equity funders to commit unless you have an agreement with Formula One,” Froneman said, while adding that Formula One would also require evidence that the project could be funded.However, he added that the property component provides a fallback should the Formula One bid not succeed, as the land could still support a high-end real estate development. “Even if you are unsuccessful with Formula One, you will still have very valuable land that underpins this that you could continue with the real estate development,” Froneman said.If successful, the Froneman estimates the project could create more than 15,000 jobs with another 8,000 people employed during race week.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia's mystery shoulder-fired missile 'Iva': Is Moscow using Chinese or Iranian MANPADS system?
articles.summary: An unusual shoulder-fired air defence missile spotted in Russian military footage may actually be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising fresh questions
articles.body: An unusual shoulder-fired air defence missile spotted in Russian military footage may actually be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising fresh questions about just how interconnected the military supply networks forming a troika between Moscow, Beijing and Tehran have become. The man-portable air defence system, or MANPADS, showed up in Russian television footage of a mobile air defence group operating in the Rostov region bordering Ukraine, during an exercise reportedly involving a unit of Russia's 51st Air Defence Division.What makes the sighting notable is that the weapon doesn't closely resemble any of the Russian-made Man Portable Air Defence System (MANPADS) families currently in service. Russian personnel were heard referring to it as "Iva," though that name alone doesn't confirm the weapon's actual origin or model, Iva means 'willow' in Russian, with one willow species named Verba, which also happens to be the name of Russia's most modern MANPADS.Closer examination of the launcher has instead drawn comparisons to both Iran's Misagh-3 and China's QW-series systems, particularly the QW-18, QW-18A and QW-19. A box-like component visible near the front of the launcher appears more consistent with photographs of the Chinese QW-series than with the Misagh, though analysts also haven't ruled out the possibility that this is simply a Russian-built derivative of a Chinese or Iranian design rather than an imported weapon outright.For context, Russia's existing MANPADS arsenal includes the Verba and the older Igla system, the latter also used by the Indian Army, deployed across terrain ranging from the Siachen Glacier to the deserts of Rajasthan. MANPADS themselves are shoulder-launched, guided surface-to-air missiles designed to threaten low-flying aircraft, particularly helicopters, and increasingly, low-flying cruise missiles and drones. They can also be fired from vehicles, tripods and warships.Within broader air defence doctrine, MANPADS function as the last line of defence in a layered, point-defence network, protecting high-value assets like command centres, airbases and forward troop positions as one of the last layers of an overlapping integrated air defence neytwork. When larger medium or long-range surface-to-air systems fail to intercept a target, or when low-altitude threats exploit terrain to dodge radar, MANPADS step in as the final tier, typically engaging targets below 10,000 to 15,000 feet in altitude and within a horizontal range of five to eight kilometers, whether that's a loitering drone, a terrain-hugging cruise missile, an attack helicopter, or a jet attempting a low-altitude strafing run. These missiles prove to be more cost effective at shooting down cheap loitering munitions when compared to bigger missiles.India, meanwhile, is developing its own heavy weight contender in this category, the Very Short Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS) a fourth-generation MANPADS built by the Research Centre Imarat in Hyderabad with support from multiple DRDO laboratories and Indian industry partners. Designed to neutralise low-altitude aerial threats at short range, the system forms part of India's broader Integrated Air Defence Weapon System and has already been through successful test firings.

articles.title: Kenya confirms first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus
articles.summary: The patient had been living in DR Congo, where more than 4,000 people have died from the disease this year.
articles.body:
Kenya has confirmed its first ever case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.

Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

Since then, all known cases of the highly infectious disease have been in DR Congo.

The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment.

​​There are however four vaccines in development, with human trials for one of them launched in July.

Duale confirmed that the Kenyan national had tested positive for the Bundibugyo species.

According to the minister, the patient first travelled by road from DR Congo to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi.

Duale said that after being taken to the Nairobi Hospital, the patient was transferred to an isolation facility that was built during the Covid-19 pandemic.

It was there that the patient "developed fever, chills, intense fatigue and weakness, painful swallowing, muscle pain and bleeding under the skin".

"Doctors suspected a viral haemorrhagic fever based on his symptoms and travel history and collected samples for testing. The sample tested positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus," Duale said.

The patient died at 23:30 (20:30 GMT) on Monday and his burial is planned for later on Tuesday in line with public health safety protocols.

At least 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers, have been identified, while health authorities are tracing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who travelled on the same flight.

A senior health ministry official said the patient might have passed screening at the airport because the medication he was taking masked his symptoms.

Kenya introduced tighter checks at airports and border posts after the outbreak was declared in DR Congo.

The health minister urged Kenyans "not to panic, as all systems are in place to mitigate the spread of the disease".

He asked health workers to be "extra vigilant and maintain the highest infection prevention and control measures regardless of the condition being treated".

The WHO has recorded 4,114 deaths out of 8,544 cases in the current outbreak, making it the largest ever recorded in DR Congo, where Ebola was first discovered in 1976.

Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) believes the current toll could be even higher because of gaps in surveillance and testing in the war-torn country.

On Monday, MSF said the virus was spreading "like a megafire", with new hotspots emerging in North Kivu province, which borders Ituri where the virus began.

Since early September this had "intensified dramatically" with the province now accounting for nearly 40% of all newly confirmed cases nationwide, MSF said.

Eastern DR Congo has been riven by decades of conflict, with multiple rebel groups operating in the region amid ethnic tensions and fighting for political power and control of lucrative natural resources.

The crisis has led to the death and displacement of millions of people, and hampered the country's ability to develop and maintain functional health care systems and infrastructure.

articles.title: Give My Head Peace creators told via email show not recommissioned
articles.summary: It comes as the BBC attempts to save £500m over two years as it faces "significant financial pressures".
articles.body:
The creators of Give My Head Peace have said they were told by email that the long-running comedy show had not been commissioned for a new series.

It comes as the corporation faces "significant financial pressures" and is attempting to save £500m over two years .

Tim McGarry, who plays Da, said the team are "disappointed" by the news and "a little bit hurt" at how they say it was delivered.

The Blame Game, which is presented by McGarry, will also not return.

A spokesperson said that while they "recognise the significant contribution" both programmes have made, the BBC is "facing real financial challenges at this time and will need to make some difficult decisions in order to manage them".

"We're slightly hurt as well in the manner of it. It was not very pleasant in that we were told by email after 30 years that Give My Head Peace wasn't coming back," McGarry told BBC Radio Ulster's Talkback programme.

"The BBC doesn't owe us a living. We've been very, very lucky, I want to make that absolutely clear, the BBC made this programme when no other broadcaster in Northern Ireland would make such a programme," he said.

"But to lose it in such a way, just kind of get an email saying sorry lads you're away is a little bit hurtful."

The news the two shows would not be returning to the BBC was first reported by the Belfast Newsletter .

Sitcom Give My Head Peace first appeared on TV in 1995 while panel show The Blame Game broadcast its 23rd series last year.

Give My Head Peace starred the comedy and writing group the Hole in the Wall Gang with characters such as Da, Ma, Uncle Andy, Cal, Billy and Dympna.

The programme started with the pilot episode Two Ceasefires and a Wedding and ran from the late 1990s to 2007.

Despite originating on TV, the team also write and perform a stage show version of Give My Head Peace and present a related podcast.

McGarry said their ability to tap into the news cycle in a comedic way has helped the show stay "relevant".

"The great thing about Give My Head Peace was it's a mixture of satire, political satire, but also farce and laugh-out-loud comedy, so kids can enjoy it, people who are into our politics can enjoy it," he said. "And I think we still did have relevance."

"Comedy is genuinely a very important force in society. We need to laugh at ourselves. We take ourselves far too seriously in this part of the world sometimes."

He added that the show had "30 good years" at the BBC, but said "one last hurrah would have been nice because this is an iconic show and much loved by very, very many people across Northern Ireland".

Damon Quinn, who plays Cal and is a writer and producer on the show, said they were "unbelievably proud" of it and "very grateful" to the BBC, but said not commissioning another season was a "misguided and wrong decision".

"There are a lot of pressures financially on the BBC these days, you can't deny that it's true, but I think if you want to defend local broadcasting, local programmes, this is not the way to defend them.

"[Give My Head Peace] is made by people who live here, it's of this place," he said.

"That's what local audiences are going to want, there's always going to be that need and a want for that."

The Blame Game was also hosted by McGarry and featured panellists such as Colin Murphy, Diona Doherty, Neil Delamere and Jake O'Kane.

Writing on social media, Murphy thanked everyone who watched and worked on the show, adding that "nothing lasts forever".

Delamere added they had a "great time over the last 20 years" and thanked people for watching the show.

Local comedian Paddy McDonnell who has appeared on the show said he is "sad to see" the cuts.

"Times do change and things have to happen, it is just unfortunate that its two of those institutions being pulled from the TV and the airwaves," he told BBC Radio Ulster's The Nolan Show .

A BBC spokesperson said: "We haven't commissioned new series of The Blame Game or Give My Head Peace at this stage.

"We recognise the significant contribution that both programmes have made to our local TV schedules over many years and the enjoyment that they've provided for BBC audiences.

"We are facing real financial challenges at this time and will need to make some difficult decisions in order to manage them, whilst also protecting the distinctiveness and impact of the service we provide."

Other shows across the BBC that have not been renewed include RuPaul's Drag Race UK , Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live at the Apollo .

articles.title: In 1934, America created a $1 conservation stamp for duck hunters; it has since helped protect more than 6 million acres of wetlands
articles.summary: In 1934, the United States introduced a small annual stamp that linked waterfowl hunting directly to wetland conservation.
articles.body: In 1934, the United States introduced a small annual stamp that linked waterfowl hunting directly to wetland conservation. The Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act, signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on 16 March that year, required waterfowl hunters aged 16 and over to buy a stamp. The first one cost $1 and featured mallards, with artwork created by conservationist and cartoonist J.N. Ding Darling. More than nine decades later, the Federal Duck Stamp has raised over $1.3 billion and helped conserve more than 6 million acres of habitat, according to the US Fish & Wildlife Service (US FWS).How the 1934 $1 Duck Stamp began protecting wetlandsThe idea emerged during a difficult period for both people and wildlife. BirdNote reported that the early 1930s were marked by the Great Depression, drought and widespread damage to wetlands. Waterfowl populations had already been weakened by hunting pressure and the loss of breeding habitat as wetlands were drained.The Federal Register provides the legal history of the programme. Congress passed the Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act on 16 March 1934, and Roosevelt signed it the same day. The law required waterfowl hunters aged 16 or older to purchase a stamp every year. The money was intended to provide a dedicated source of funding for protecting habitat.The first stamp was designed by Jay N. Ding Darling, who was then director of the Bureau of Biological Survey, the predecessor of the US Fish & Wildlife Service. The US FWS says Darling's design began an annual tradition in which wildlife art became part of a conservation funding system.The hunting requirement became a conservation toolThe unusual feature of the programme was its direct connection between hunting and habitat protection. Hunters were the main group required to purchase the stamp, turning an annual hunting requirement into a source of money for wetlands.According to the Federal Register, the programme had generated more than $1 billion by 2018 and supported conservation of more than 6 million acres of waterfowl habitat. The agency also noted that the protected areas benefit many species beyond waterfowl, while wetlands can help with flood control and water purification.The US FWS now reports that more than $1.3 billion has been raised since 1934. Its Federal Duck Stamp programme states that 98 cents of every dollar spent goes towards acquiring vital habitat or conservation easements within the National Wildlife Refuge System.How Duck Stamp money reaches wildlife habitatThe funds do not simply support the production of the stamp. They are deposited into the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund, which is used to purchase or lease wetlands and other wildlife habitat.The US FWS explains that more than 6 million acres have been acquired using Federal Duck Stamp revenue. More than 300 national wildlife refuges have been created or expanded with the help of these funds, while at least one refuge in nearly every state has benefited.The programme also supports smaller wetlands and surrounding uplands through Waterfowl Production Areas. These sites can provide important breeding and nesting habitat, while conservation easements can protect land without necessarily ending private ownership or its working-land uses.What makes the stamp useful beyond huntingThe stamp's value extends beyond the people who are legally required to buy it. The US FWS says anyone can purchase a Federal Duck Stamp, including conservationists, birdwatchers and collectors. A current signed stamp can also provide free admission to national wildlife refuges that charge an entrance fee.The wetlands protected through the programme have practical benefits as well. According to the US FWS, they can help purify water, control floods and reduce soil erosion and sedimentation. They also create opportunities for outdoor recreation.The National Wildlife Federation reported in 2026 that more than 98 percent of Duck Stamp proceeds go directly towards acquiring and protecting wetland habitat for the National Wildlife Refuge System.The artwork has become part of the programmeThe conservation story is also tied to wildlife art. The first Federal Duck Stamp Contest was held in 1949, when 65 artists submitted 88 designs. The Federal Register notes that it remains the only art competition of its kind sponsored by the US government.Today, the US FWS holds the annual competition, with the winning artwork becoming the design for the following year's stamp. The contest gives the programme a changing visual identity while keeping wildlife at its centre.The designs have also evolved alongside the programme. The Federal Register records changes intended to reinforce the connection between the stamp, waterfowl hunting heritage and conservation. Artists are required to work within rules governing eligible waterfowl and the overall theme.The scale of the programme has changed considerably since that first $1 stamp. BirdNote recorded that by 2014, Duck Stamp sales had raised about $900 million and helped save or create 5.5 million acres of wetland, riparian and grassland habitat.You use AI every day. articles.title: An American citizen was arrested at airport by Border security for wiping his phone with PIN; Federal judge approves search without warrant; here's what new ruling says on phone and laptop searches
articles.summary: US border agents can search people’s phones and other electronic devices without a warrant or any suspicion, a federal judge has ruled.
articles.body: US border agents can search people’s phones and other electronic devices without a warrant or any suspicion, a federal judge has ruled. In a ruling last month, the US Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit said that border agents do not need reasonable suspicion before manually searching a traveller's cellphone at the border. The ruling comes months after an Atlanta resident, Samuel Tunick was arrested on charges of destruction of property for wiping his phone with PIN during airport search. Prosecutors then accused Tunick of destroying potential evidence. The latest ruling stemmed from a bank fraud and money laundering case against a man in New York City in 2024.What the court saidWriting in the 2nd Circuit’s majority opinion, Judge Steven J. Menashi said that border agents in the case stated above and others can “manually” look through someone’s phone or other device without needing to give a reason. In the ruling, Menashi said that there should be no distinction between a phone and other types of property, equating it to luggage or a notebook.“Because a cellphone is property, our precedents establish that the government does not need to have reasonable suspicion before searching a traveler’s cellphone at the border,” he wrote.What was the Atlanta case where man wiped his phone with PINAs reported by The Guardian, Samuel Lutnick’s case centred on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices. These include the ability to erase a device by entering a designated passcode. The incident occurred at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24, after Tunick returned from the Dominican Republic. Tunick’s attorneys confirmed GrapheneOS was running on his phone.Agents repeatedly asked Tunick to unlock his phone and warned that it would be seized if he refused. After he eventually provided a passcode, “the screen went blank, flashed several times, and the phone appeared to restart,” according to the defence motion. Data stored on the device was subsequently lost. Prosecutors then alleged that the wipe was a deliberate attempt to destroy potential evidence. Tunick’s lawyers maintain that the underlying search violated his constitutional rights. The GrapheneOS has a feature that allows the device owner to set a passcode that deliberately wipes the contents of that device if entered instead of the user’s unlock passcode.Here’s what U.S. Customs and Border Protection said about border search of electronic devices at ports of entryU.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our nation’s borders and enforcing numerous laws at U.S. ports of entry. CBP’s ability to lawfully inspect electronic devices crossing the border is integral to keeping America safe in an increasingly digital world.All travelers crossing the United States border are subject to CBP inspection. On rare occasions, CBP officers may search a traveler’s mobile phone, computer, camera, or other electronic devices during the inspection process. These searches have been used to identify and combat terrorist activity, drug smuggling, human smuggling, bulk cash smuggling, human trafficking, intellectual property rights violations and visa fraud, among other violations. They enable the discovery of digital contraband, such as child pornography, illicit transfer of restricted or classified information, or other export-controlled information. Furthermore, border searches of electronic devices are often integral to determining an individual’s intentions upon entry to the United States and thus provide additional information relevant to admissibility of foreign nationals under U.S. immigration laws.CBP has established strict guidelines, above and beyond prevailing legal requirements, to ensure that these searches are exercised judiciously and responsibly and are consistent with the public trust.The number of travelers crossing the border that experience a border search of their electronic devices is small. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, less than 0.01 percent of arriving international travelers encountered by CBP at a port of entry had their electronic devices searched. Additional statistics are available in the Frequently Asked Questions below and Relevant Policies and Documents box to the right of this page.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'ASOS hacked': App users receive notifications apparently sent by hackers
articles.summary: Dozens of people appear to have received a strange message from the clothing and beauty store's app.
articles.body:
Asos users across the UK have been sent pop-up messages from its app that appear to have been sent by hackers trying to extort the company.

Dozens of people have told the BBC about receiving a strange message from the clothing and beauty store's app, appearing on their phone screens.

"Dear ASOS DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it," the message reads.

Asos did not immediately respond to the BBC's requests for comment.

"If confirmed, this is a deeply serious attack because the hackers appear to have done something particularly brazen: turned ASOS's own app into their ransom note," says Charlotte Wilson, head of enterprise at cyber-security firm Check Point.

"Millions of people trust notifications from apps on their phones because they are supposed to come directly from the company."

On social media, dozens of people have posted about receiving the message - confused as to what it means.

Although the apparent extortion message has been issued directly to customers, it is addressed to Asos' data protection officer (DPO) and IT team.

The message claims the unnamed hackers have "fully compromised the Snowflake instance".

This refers to the data storage company Snowflake, whose tools are used by dozens of firms for collecting, analysing and storing data.

It is not known if ASOS is a customer of Snowflake or what data, if any, is stored with the service.

But Snowflake has been the subject of many high profile data breaches in recent years and has been linked to incidents targeting services including Ticketmaster and Santander .

It is, however, very unusual for a data breach to be revealed quite so publicly - and for customers to be informed in this manner.

Most extortions and negotiations by cyber criminals are conducted in private, with hackers hoping their discretion will result in a quiet pay-off.

The pop up message contains a link to the hackers' Telegram channel.

The new group is calling itself Xuanye Group and only created its Telegram channel today.

They have posted only three times with the latest being about the ASOS hack.

Dan Bird, from cyber security firm Horizon3 says the pop up message the criminals sent implies that their access has gone beyond the Snowflake database.

"Sending a push notification to ASOS's app users would require access to the company's notification system, which is separate from the Snowflake data platform the attackers claim to have compromised."

"If both claims hold up, it suggests the attackers got hold of credentials that opened more than one door," he said.

articles.title: York tourism down as visitor numbers fall
articles.summary: York sees attraction visits and city footfall drop, according to figures for the first half of 2026.
articles.body:
Visits to York's tourist attractions and city centre footfall have both declined so far this year compared with 2025, new figures show.

Data published by tourism body Make It York showed city footfall monitors recorded 15.08 million visits between January and June, down 8% compared with the same period last year.

Visits to attractions also fell by 17% year-on-year during the first half of 2026.

However, the report suggested there were signs of improvement during the spring and early summer, with attraction visits increasing and some parts of the city recording higher footfall.

Footfall figures are based on electronic monitoring equipment which records pedestrian movements at locations across the city centre and do not represent individual visitors.

The figures are contained in an update on Make It York's work which is due to be discussed by councillors on 12 October.

Data showed footfall on Parliament Street fell by 28% in the first half of the year compared with 2025, although visitor numbers there increased by 5% in June.

Micklegate bucked the trend, recording a 1% rise in footfall during the first six months of the year and a 4% increase between April and June.

Visits to major attractions including Clifford's Tower and the National Railway Museum fell year-on-year, while smaller attractions saw a steeper drop.

Separate figures showed York attracted 8.8 million visitors in 2025, fewer than the previous year and below pre-pandemic levels.

According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service international visitors accounted for 18% of the total, up from 14% a year earlier, while overnight stays also increased.
