articles.title: Animal rights group seeks probe into death of Pallatt Brahmadathan
articles.summary: Animal rights group urges probe into captive elephant Pallatt Brahmadathan’s lightning death, seeking audits and mandatory lightning protection in Kerala shelters.
articles.body: Kochi: Daya Animal Welfare Organization has urged authorities not to dismiss the death of captive elephant Pallatt Brahmadathan from lightning as merely a natural disaster and demanded an inquiry into the shelter’s safety measures and maintenance standards.The organisation demanded an expert evaluation of whether adequate safety was provided to the elephant, which was tied with heavy iron chains during severe rain and lightning.“We demand a probe into the circumstances surrounding Brahmadathan’s death and the public disclosure of its findings. The investigation must inspect the temporary shelter’s structure, grounding systems, lightning protection and the chains used to tether the animal,” it said in a statement.The organisation called on the forest department to establish a strict safety protocol for housing captive elephants during extreme weather conditions. It advocated making scientific lightning protection and proper grounding systems mandatory in tethering locations across the state.Additionally, the organisation requested urgent safety audits of all captive elephant shelters in Keralam to identify and eliminate potential hazards. It asked authorities to amend current elephant management rules to include specific safety standards tailored for harsh weather conditions.The petition highlighted a similar incident in 2014 when another elephant, Chirakkadavu Krishnankutty, died in similar circumstances.“Past incidents must be thoroughly analysed to create comprehensive safety guidelines,” it said in the petition submitted to the chief conservator of forests and the minister for forests.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.summary: Rift in Rashtriya Lok Morcha surfaces as 3 of 4 RLM MLAs back Ram Pukar Sinha for Saran teachers’ seat against NDA’s JD(U) nominee Anand Pushkar.
articles.body: Patna: Internal differences within the Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) became public on Tuesday over the party’s stand in the legislative council elections, with three of the four RLM MLAs openly backing Ram Pukar Sinha against the NDA nominee in the Saran teachers’ constituency.RLM national general secretary and Madhubani MLA Madhav Anand on Tuesday reiterated his support for Sinha, the party’s state general secretary, and said he had conveyed his position to party chief Upendra Kushwaha.The other two MLAs backing Sinha are RLM state president and Dinara MLA Alok Kumar Singh and Bajpatti MLA Rameshwar Mahto. articles.title: BCCI seeks Ajit Agarkar replacement: Explaining how new selector can trump Pragyan Ojha for India Chief Selector role
articles.summary: Here's how Ajit Agarkar's replacement from West Zone can trump Pragyan Ojha for the role of BCCI chief selector.
articles.body:
The BCCI has invited applications for one vacant seat on the Men's Selection Committee, with the window open until October 14.

Per the board's zonal rotation policy, the new member will come from the West Zone, the zone Ajit Agarkar represented.

If the chosen candidate has played more Tests for India than Pragyan Ojha's 24, they could leapfrog him to become chief selector.

BCCI opens applications for Ajit Agarkar's vacant selector seat

The BCCI has formally invited applications for one position on its Men's Selection Committee, confirming in a media advisory dated October 6 that the vacancy follows Ajit Agarkar's exit from the panel. The board has set the deadline for submissions at 5:00 p.m. IST on October 14.

The eligibility bar is familiar : a minimum of 7 Tests, or 30 First-Class matches, or 10 ODIs plus 20 First-Class games, with a mandatory five-year gap since retirement. Shortlisted applicants will then be called in for personal interviews before a final call is made. Journalist Vikrant Gupta added further context to the process.

He noted that the incoming selector must represent the same zone as Agarkar, and that the candidate ultimately selected will directly decide who chairs the committee.

Why should Ajit Agarkar's replacement be specifically from the West Zone?

The BCCI's selection committee runs on a strict zonal structure, with one representative from each of the North, South, East, West, and Central zones. Agarkar, a Mumbai cricketer, occupied the West Zone seat for his entire tenure as chairman, so his departure leaves that specific regional slot empty rather than a free-for-all opening.

Under this system, the board cannot simply pick any eligible former cricketer; the replacement must hail from a West Zone association such as Mumbai, Gujarat, Saurashtra, Baroda, Maharashtra, or Vidarbha.

It is this same zonal math that puts Pragyan Ojha's position under the microscope, since he already sits on the committee from the South Zone, and the incoming West Zone member's own Test résumé will decide whether he keeps the chairman's chair or hands it over.

The other members in the committee include Shiv Sunder Das (Central Zone), who has played 23 Tests, R.P. Singh (Central/North Zone) who has played 14 Tests and Ajay Ratra (North Zone), who has played six Tests for the country.

West Zone candidates who can trump Pragyan Ojha for BCCI chief selector role

Ojha's own international résumé, 24 Tests, sets the bar any incoming West Zone selector needs to clear to take over as chairman outright. Several names already doing the rounds comfortably clear that mark.

Parthiv Patel remains the most widely reported frontrunner, having already been linked to the West Zone seat previously. The former wicketkeeper played 25 Tests for India, one more than Ojha, which would be enough on its own to hand him the chairmanship if he is the one appointed.

Irfan Pathan , the former Baroda all-rounder, played 29 Tests across his India career and comfortably meets the experience and retirement criteria, making him another West Zone name who would outrank Ojha on caps alone.

Wasim Jaffer , the prolific Mumbai opener, played 31 Tests for India and has remained closely involved in domestic coaching and commentary since retiring, giving him both the eligibility and the Test tally to leapfrog Ojha.

Zaheer Khan represents the heavyweight option, with 92 Tests to his name from a long new-ball career for Mumbai and India. His name has previously done the rounds for the chief selector's post itself, and his Test pedigree would leave Ojha's tally far behind if he were to apply.

However, given that he has already taken the CSK head coach role, it looks highly unlikely unless he abandons it for the selection committee.

With the committee seat now formally open and the clock ticking toward the October 14 deadline, the next fortnight promises to be a closely watched stretch for Indian cricket's backroom.
